clue.text: Much read setter for one that's equipped to listen

blocks.note: a setter is a breed of dog, 'for one' marking it as an example
having ears, so fitted out for hearing

explanation.surface: A crossword setter is pictured as a widely read figure, as though a famous author had a big audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the puzzle compiler, but here it is the gundog.
explanation.definitionFit: A book thumbed so often that its page corners are folded down is one that has been read a great deal.

clue.text: Some think fine lines reveal life there  …

definitions.text: Some think fine lines reveal life there

blocks.clueFragment: Some think fine lines reveal life there
blocks.note: surface reading: a remark about poetry, where a few well-chosen lines can bring life to a page
setter's reading: fortune tellers read the creases of the hand, including the so-called life line

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a few elegant lines of verse can show what life is about.
explanation.walkthrough: Palmistry reads the lines on the inner hand, one of which is called the life line; 'Some' hints that not everyone believes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner surface of the hand is where palmists claim to see the life line and others.

clue.text: …  a projected life perhaps

blocks.note: surface reading: a life planned or forecast ahead, continuing the thought of the previous clue
setter's reading: projected onto a cinema screen, so a life story shown as a film

explanation.surface: Following on from palm reading, a life foretold or anticipated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Projected' sounds like forecast, but it means thrown onto a screen by a projector.
explanation.definitionFit: A biographical film tells a real person's life story and is shown by projection in cinemas.

clue.text: Reluctant agreement to get extremely fit

blocks.note: a plain synonym
fit as in healthy

explanation.surface: Someone grudgingly agrees to a demanding fitness regime.
explanation.definitionFit: Said with a sigh, the phrase is a grudging way of saying yes to something.

clue.text: Snores warn about constriction

indicators.note: about can mean all around or in disarray, so the letters are turned every which way

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Snoring is a warning sign of a tightened airway, a medical-sounding observation.
explanation.definitionFit: Constriction is the state of being squeezed tight, which is lack of width.

clue.text: One rejects measure of silk

blocks.note: first meaning: a person who denies or refuses something
second meaning: a unit of fineness for silk, nylon and other yarns, as on stocking packets

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings are pronounced differently: one rhymes with 'fire', the yarn unit is said 'den-ear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who denies a claim rejects it, and a denier is a weight-per-length unit used to grade silk thread.

clue.text: Vetoing a change to side with the locals

indicators.note: a change of form means the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A colonial official overrules a policy change in order to back the local population.
explanation.definitionFit: To go native is to adopt the ways and loyalties of the people where one is posted.

clue.text: A bit upset at seeing return for property

indicators.note: only a small piece of the following words is wanted, lifted straight out of them
to return is to go back the way you came, so the run of letters is read right to left

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word, the whole second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Someone is a little upset at seeing a payback on an investment in land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like the reversal signal but is only part of the hiding place; 'return' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a large piece of land or the sum of someone's possessions, both kinds of property.

clue.text: Took out part of chapter as editor

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is wanted, lifted straight from them

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the three words

explanation.surface: An editor cuts a section from a book's chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase something is to remove or delete it, so took out fits as a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Starts training eleven athletic men to be one

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so each word gives its initial

blocks.note: the initials of the four words

explanation.surface: A coach starts drilling eleven sportsmen so they act as a single unit.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder words also describe the answer: a football or cricket side has eleven players.
explanation.definitionFit: A side acting together is a single unit, which is the sense of one here.

clue.text: Eccentric coach to teach kids to hold it

blocks.note: potty is British slang for mad or crazy
a verb synonym: to coach is to train

explanation.surface: An oddball sports coach is assigned to teach children ball-holding skills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a bus, and 'hold it' sounds like a ball; both are about toddlers and toilets.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilet training a toddler means teaching them bladder control until they can reach the pot.

clue.text: Funny girl cons rich couples at the centre

indicators.note: couples are pairs, and at the centre means taking the two letters from the middle of each word

blocks.note: the two middle letters
the two middle letters
the two middle letters

explanation.surface: A comic woman fleeces wealthy pairs of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironic humour is wry or droll, so funny in the sense of amusing through contradiction.

clue.text: Idea in town spread across the country

indicators.note: spread out means scattered, so the letters are dispersed and rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A notion born in one town catches on throughout the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nationwide extends over the whole nation, which is the sense of covering all the country.

clue.text: The press mostly give it three stars

definitions.text: The press mostly give it three stars

blocks.clueFragment: The press mostly give it three stars
blocks.note: surface reading: critics mostly award a film or show a three-star review
setter's reading: newspapers print a certain expletive as its first letter followed by three asterisks

explanation.surface: Reviewers broadly agree on a middling three-star rating for something.
explanation.walkthrough: The stars are asterisks, not a rating: papers censor the swear word by starring out its last three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The euphemism names a four-letter swear word that print journalism routinely asterisks out.

clue.text: Mark time when senior moments become the norm

definitions.text: when senior moments become the norm

blocks.note: a dot is a small mark
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone notes the point when forgetfulness becomes routine.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'senior moment' is a jokey phrase for an elderly lapse of memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotage is the period of old age marked by declining memory and faculties, when such lapses are routine.

clue.text: This paper makes a university take on graduate

indicators.note: to take on is to admit or absorb, so one piece holds the other inside it

blocks.note: a common abbreviation
taken as written
the everyday short form

explanation.surface: A newspaper is described as a university hiring a graduate.
explanation.walkthrough: The Graun or Grauniad is the satirical magazine Private Eye's nickname for the Guardian, which publishes this puzzle, mocking its old reputation for misprints.
explanation.definitionFit: Grauniad is the long-standing mocking nickname for the Guardian newspaper, here the paper hosting the crossword.

clue.text: Patron makes charge in court

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: CT is the standard abbreviation for court
a lien is a legal charge or claim on property

explanation.surface: A sponsor brings a legal action before the judges.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron of a shop or professional is a customer, someone who pays for services.

clue.text: Used to clean litter you endlessly scattered

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for a noun answer: a thing used to clean

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word is cut off
things scattered are thrown about, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: Something a person used for cleaning up, dropped as rubbish all over the place.
explanation.definitionFit: A toiletry is any article such as soap or shampoo that serves for washing and grooming.

clue.text: Approves party in small apartments

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: small signals the abbreviation for apartments
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A residents' committee gives the go-ahead to a party in tiny flats.
explanation.definitionFit: A council or meeting that adopts a proposal formally accepts and endorses it.

clue.text: Legal nod for redevelopment of bricked-up resort

indicators.note: redeveloping a site rebuilds it in a new layout, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Planners give legal approval to rebuilding a boarded-up holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bricked-up' suggests sealed off, but it means built out of toy bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme park chain is built largely from the famous plastic toy bricks, so it is a resort made of bricks.

clue.text: Afraid to drop leading female for scolding

indicators.note: dropping the leading letter means removing the first one

blocks.note: a synonym
F is the standard abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: Someone is scared that losing the senior woman will mean being told off.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter of the synonym happens to be the female abbreviation, so it is that F which is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: An earful is a long angry telling-off, so it is an idiom for a scolding.

clue.text: Try taking wee word back to informer

definitions.note: informer in the loose sense of someone who passes on news

indicators.note: going back means reading the word from its end to its start

blocks.note: a go is a try or attempt
a vulgar word for urine, which wee also means

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to take a children's word for urinating back to a police informant.
explanation.definitionFit: A gossip spreads news about others, someone who passes on information, loosely an informer.

clue.text: Information age types  …

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
an era is an age

explanation.surface: A sociologist classifies the different kinds of people in the information age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Information age' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Genera are biological groupings, the plural of genus, so they are classes or types.

clue.text: Tack required when priming grenade  …

blocks.note: first meaning: a short flat-headed pin for fixing paper to a board
second meaning: read as two words, the act of pulling out the safety pin that arms a hand grenade

explanation.walkthrough: A drawing pin is the British name for a thumbtack; the second reading splits the phrase into 'drawing' (pulling out) and 'pin'.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a thumbtack, and taken literally describes pulling the safety pin before throwing a grenade.

clue.text: …  not many sound relieved

definitions.note: the answer is an exclamation one makes when relieved

indicators.note: sound means the word is identified by how it is said, not how it is written

blocks.note: not many is a small number

explanation.surface: Following the grenade, only a few people sound relieved.
explanation.definitionFit: Phew is the exclamation of someone relieved that a danger or strain has passed.

clue.text: …  turn up with very loud promotion

indicators.note: turning something round sends it the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
fortissimo, marked ff in music

explanation.surface: Turning up the volume to advertise something loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: A puff is a piece of overblown praise used to advertise a product, a promotional plug.

clue.text: Old teacher had trouble following friend

indicators.note: something in trouble is in disorder, so the letters are muddled

blocks.note: bud is informal for a friend
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly tutor got into difficulty after his pal did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the jumbled word after the friend.
explanation.definitionFit: The founder of Buddhism was an ancient spiritual teacher, so an old teacher.

clue.text: OK, let go! It's bound to win

blocks.note: sure as a casual yes
to let an employee go is to fire them

explanation.surface: A tipster urges someone to place the bet because the horse cannot lose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let go' suggests releasing a racehorse, but it means dismissing a worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A sure-fire bet or plan is certain to succeed, which is what bound to win describes.
